vo: Part six: one shared brain. We built each Bot on its own. But right now they don't talk. What lands in your inbox never reaches marketing. What marketing finds never reaches sales.
And when a customer finally comes on board, the sales conversation should travel with them. Otherwise, the client has to explain everything twice.
Imagine every surgeon who does one kind of operation sharing everything they learn with every other surgeon, at the click of a button. That's the idea: one shared brain.
Your Bots are only as good as what they know about your business. The most valuable thing you own is how you do things differently from everyone else. That has to live in one place.
First, put your whole business in one place: your email, calendar, calls, customer records, and documents. That's your data.
Second, connect every Bot to it, whichever tool each one runs on. They all get your context right away.
Start with one handoff, and add more once it works. Every Friday, sales saves the top objections. On Monday, marketing turns them into next week's content.
The inbox Bot knows your voice, so it can write sales follow-ups. The delivery Bot reads promises made in sales and builds a punch list, so nothing gets dropped when a client arrives.
You can build this brain yourself, but it takes time, and it can break. A ready-made platform is faster. The point is this: tools change every week, but your brain stays the same.
So, the whole ladder. Find a painkiller. Then inbox, delivery, marketing, and sales. Then one brain to connect them all, so each new customer gets taken care of without you.

There's one thing a Bot will never do: have a vision for what you want to create. Make it big enough for your dreams and goals to fit inside. The better you hold it, the faster you pull that future toward you.
That's why the future belongs to one person with a whole lot of agents. Tell me what stood out. And this week, start with the inbox.
